papers.title: Power- and Fragmentation-aware Online Scheduling for GPU Datacenters
authors: Francesco Lettich, Emanuele Carlini, Franco Maria Nardini, Raffaele Perego, Salvatore Trani
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2412.17484v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The rise of Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models is driving increased GPU usage in data centers for complex training and inference tasks, impacting operational costs, energy demands, and the environmental footprint of large-scale computing infrastructures. This work addresses the online scheduling problem in GPU datacenters, which involves scheduling tasks without knowledge of their future arrivals. We focus on two objectives: minimizing GPU fragmentation and reducing power consumption. GPU fragmentation occurs when partial GPU allocations hinder the efficient use of remaining resources, especially as the datacenter nears full capacity. papers.title: Toward Open ISA Supercomputing: A Comparative Study of RISC-V, Arm, and x86 Architectures on HPC Workloads
authors: Emanuele Venieri, Giacomo Madella, Gabriele Ceccolini, Simone Manoni, Federico Ficarelli, Filippo Barbari, Jenny Lynn Almerol, Elisabetta Boella, Nitin Shukla, Simone Bn\`a, Luca Benini, Andrea bartolini
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2610.32632v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: RISC-V is emerging as a candidate architecture for high-performance computing (HPC), but its competitiveness against established x86 and Arm processors remains difficult to assess because existing studies use different platforms, workloads, and methodologies, and rarely consider energy efficiency. Our work provides an evaluation of contemporary HPC RISC-V, Arm, and x86 processors using a common software stack and methodology. We characterize the Sophgo SG2044 and compare it with the NVIDIA Grace CPU Superchip and Intel Xeon Platinum 8480+ across four HPC benchmarks (STREAM, HPL, HPL-MxP, and HPCG) and four representative applications (iPIC3D, PLUTO, OpenFOAM, and llama.cpp). papers.title: Data Quality Audit and Bivariate Temperature-Humidity Analysis of a Long-Term LoRaWAN Network: Anomaly Detection, PCA, Clustering and Machine Learning
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2610.32438v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Long-term environmental IoT/LPWAN deployments often aggregate heterogeneous data streams from diverse devices without systematic auditing of each variable's actual coverage prior to analysis-an increased risk when multiple sensor types coexist within the same network. This work proposes a C++17 processing pipeline applied to the Tour Perret LoRaWAN dataset (421 937 frames, June 2021--June 2023, 5 devices). A systematic coverage audit integrated into the extraction phase reveals that CO2 is completely missing (0% coverage) and pressure is reported only by an isolated base module (Wyres, 4.24% of the corpus), invalidating the initial hypothesis of a joint four-variable analysis. papers.title: Bounding Queue Waits for Fair Scheduling of Bursty HPC Workloads via Hierarchical Algorithms
authors: Karaen Senthilkumar, Suman Raj, Maxime Gonthier, Kyle Chard, Donpaul Stephens, Ian Foster
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2610.32027v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: HPC clusters are shared among many projects, each holding an allocation of node-hours, and ensuring fairness is becoming harder. Foundation models workflows and automated pipelines have made job submissions bursty and concentrated among a few heavy users, so occasional users absorb queueing delays created by frequent ones, with no indication of how long their jobs will wait. Existing schedulers either forget past usage, protect only the job at the head of the queue, or assume that running jobs can be preempted. We propose HyDRA, a Hybrid Deadline and Ranking-Aware scheduler that enforces fairness among users while bounding the queue wait of every job. papers.title: MetaDB: Putting File-System Structure Back into Distributed Databases
authors: Zebin Ren, Biao Cao, Kang Chen, Zhihui Yin, Qiushi Chen, Jielong Jian, Jiwei Xiong, Xinxing Wang, Yan Xing, Liguo Duan, Ran Zheng, Xianjun Meng, Zhenyu Hou
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2610.32247v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Storage systems in production increasingly rely on distributed databases for metadata management, yet our experience at Baidu shows that treating a general-purpose database as a black box leaves substantial performance and efficiency untapped. File-system metadata exhibits directory-tree locality, differentiated consistency requirements, and clustered deletions that general-purpose databases largely ignore. We thus propose MetaDB, a metadata-aware distributed transactional database that serves as the shared metadata layer for Baidu's large-scale storage systems. MetaDB addresses three key mismatches between general-purpose databases and metadata workloads: Data Model Mismatch, Transaction Model Mismatch, and Storage Implementation Mismatch
